title: PTE Academic Listening — Practice Test 2
topic: Mixed academic topics (one per item, as in the real test)
instructions: Each item has its own recording. Audio plays automatically when you reach an item.

questions.audioScript: Desert plants have evolved unique photosynthetic pathways to conserve water in arid environments. Most plants use C3 photosynthesis, but succulents employ CAM photosynthesis, opening stomata at night when temperatures are cooler. This minimizes water loss while still capturing carbon dioxide. Some desert plants also reduce their leaf surface area to decrease transpiration. These adaptations allow plants like agave and certain cacti to thrive in extremely dry conditions with minimal water availability.
questions.modelAnswer: Desert plants employ specialized photosynthesis methods to conserve water. CAM photosynthesis allows plants like succulents to open stomata at night, reducing water loss while capturing carbon dioxide. Plants also reduce leaf area to minimize transpiration. These adaptations enable survival in arid conditions with scarce water.

questions.topic: Medieval Trade Routes and Silk Road Commerce
questions.prompt: Item 2: Medieval Trade Routes and Silk Road Commerce
questions.audioScript: The Silk Road was not a single road but a network of trade routes connecting East Asia with Europe and the Mediterranean. Traders exchanged silk, spices, ceramics, and metals across these routes. The network flourished between the second century BC and the fifteenth century. Beyond goods, ideas, religions, and technologies traveled along these routes. Buddhism and Islam spread through trade interactions. The routes declined when European maritime exploration offered faster sea routes to Asia.
questions.modelAnswer: The Silk Road was a trade network linking East Asia to Europe, operating from the second century BC to the fifteenth century. Merchants exchanged goods including silk, spices, and ceramics. Beyond commerce, religions, ideas, and technologies spread along the routes. Maritime exploration eventually replaced the overland trade network.

questions.audioScript: Renaissance humanism emphasized individual potential and classical learning. Scholars studied ancient Greek and Roman texts to rediscover forgotten knowledge. Humanism valued critical thinking and empirical observation over pure faith. Leonardo da Vinci exemplified Renaissance ideals through art, science, and engineering. The printing press enabled rapid dissemination of humanistic ideas. Patronage by wealthy families supported artists and scholars. This intellectual movement challenged medieval worldviews and laid groundwork for the Scientific Revolution.
questions.question: According to the speaker, which TWO aspects of Renaissance humanism are accurate?
options: It rejected all classical learning
It valued critical thinking and observation
It relied exclusively on religious faith
The printing press spread humanistic ideas
Medieval traditions remained unchanged
correctAnswers: It valued critical thinking and observation
The printing press spread humanistic ideas
questions.explanation: The speaker states humanism valued critical thinking and empirical observation, and explicitly mentions the printing press's role in disseminating ideas.
questions.prompt: Item 3: Renaissance Humanism and Cultural Shift

questions.audioScript: Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose. The process occurs in two main stages: light-dependent reactions in the thylakoid and light-independent reactions in the stroma. During light reactions, chlorophyll absorbs photons, splitting water and releasing oxygen. Light-independent reactions, or the Calvin cycle, fix carbon dioxide into glucose. Only about 1-2 percent of incident light energy converts to plant biomass. Factors like light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration, and temperature affect photosynthetic rate.
questions.question: According to the speaker, which TWO statements accurately describe photosynthesis?
options: Photosynthesis occurs entirely in the stroma
Chlorophyll absorbs photons during light reactions
Carbon dioxide is fixed in the Calvin cycle
Photosynthesis achieves 50 percent energy conversion
Oxygen is produced from carbon dioxide splitting
correctAnswers: Chlorophyll absorbs photons during light reactions
Carbon dioxide is fixed in the Calvin cycle
questions.explanation: The speaker correctly describes light reactions involving chlorophyll and photons, and mentions the Calvin cycle for carbon fixation.

Item 5: Particle Physics and Quantum Mechanics
questions.audioScript: Particle physics studies fundamental constituents of matter at the smallest scales. The Standard model describes quarks and leptons as basic building blocks. Subatomic particles are held together by fundamental forces carried by force-carrying particles. The discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012 confirmed theories predicting how particles acquire mass through interaction with an energy field.
questions.transcript: Particle physics studies fundamental constituents of matter at the smallest scales. The __1__ model describes quarks and leptons as basic building blocks. Subatomic particles are held together by fundamental forces carried by __2__ particles. The discovery of the Higgs __3__ in 2012 confirmed theories predicting how particles acquire mass through interaction with an energy field.

questions.audioScript: Tropical rainforests contain approximately half of Earth's terrestrial species despite covering only seven percent of land. The dense canopy of plants creates multiple layers where different species have evolved specialized roles. Trees compete for limited light by growing tall, while lianas and epiphytes use other plants for access. The rich soil is paradoxically fragile because nutrients are rapidly absorbed by living plants; decomposed material is recycled quickly by decomposers and fungi.

questions.audioScript: The Industrial Revolution transformed production from craft-based to mechanized manufacturing. The steam engine, invented by James Watt, powered machines and transportation, providing mechanical energy previously unavailable on such scales. Textile mills combined multiple production steps in one location, dramatically increasing output per worker. Factory systems relied on division of labor performing repetitive tasks, establishing the modern industrial workforce structure.

questions.audioScript: The cardiovascular system maintains blood pressure and circulation through regulatory mechanisms. Baroreceptors detect blood pressure changes and signal the brain to adjust heart rate and vessel diameter. The sympathetic nervous system increases heart rate during stress, while the parasympathetic system promotes rest. Hormones like epinephrine regulate cardiovascular responses. These integrated systems maintain homeostasis under varying physiological conditions.
options: The cardiovascular system maintains homeostasis through baroreceptors and nervous system signals that regulate heart rate and vessel diameter.
Blood pressure regulation occurs automatically without any neural or hormonal input, relying only on mechanical blood flow.
The sympathetic nervous system exclusively promotes relaxation while parasympathetic activation increases all cardiovascular activity.
questions.correctAnswer: The cardiovascular system maintains homeostasis through baroreceptors and nervous system signals that regulate heart rate and vessel diameter.
questions.explanation: The speaker describes baroreceptors detecting pressure changes and nervous system adjustment of heart rate and vessel diameter.

questions.audioScript: Biotechnology harnesses microorganisms and enzymes for industrial manufacturing. Fermentation produces ethanol, dairy products, and antibiotics using bacterial or fungal cultures. Enzyme-based processes break down biomass into usable chemicals and fuels. Genetic engineering optimizes organisms for specific production tasks. Bioreactors provide controlled environments maximizing productivity. These processes offer environmentally friendly alternatives to petroleum-based manufacturing.
options: Industrial biotechnology uses microorganisms and enzymes in fermentation and genetic engineering to produce chemicals and fuels sustainably.
Biotechnology relies exclusively on natural microorganisms without modification, making industrial applications impossible to optimize.
Chemical synthesis from petroleum remains more environmentally friendly than any biotechnological manufacturing process.
questions.correctAnswer: Industrial biotechnology uses microorganisms and enzymes in fermentation and genetic engineering to produce chemicals and fuels sustainably.
questions.explanation: The speaker describes fermentation, enzyme processes, and genetic engineering for sustainable production alternatives.

questions.audioScript: Astronomers detect exoplanets through multiple methods revealing different planetary properties. The transit method detects planets by measuring light dimming as planets pass in front of their stars. Radial velocity methods detect planetary gravity causing slight stellar motion toward and away from Earth. Direct imaging captures light reflected from planets, possible only for massive planets around young stars. Microlensing uses gravitational lensing to detect distant planets. Each method reveals different information about planetary mass, orbit, and composition.
questions.question: What is the main advantage of the transit method for exoplanet detection?
options: It reveals a planet's chemical composition through spectroscopy
It detects planets by measuring light dimming as they pass in front of stars
It works for all planets including those far from their stars
It eliminates the need for other detection methods
questions.correctAnswer: It detects planets by measuring light dimming as they pass in front of stars
questions.explanation: The speaker describes the transit method as detecting planets through light dimming during stellar passage.

questions.audioScript: Mitochondria generate ATP through oxidative phosphorylation, the primary energy source for cellular work. The electron transport chain transfers electrons through protein complexes embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane. This process pumps protons creating a concentration gradient. ATP synthase harnesses the proton gradient to phosphorylate ADP to ATP. Approximately 30-32 ATP molecules are produced per glucose molecule. Mutations in mitochondrial genes cause genetic diseases affecting high-energy organs like muscle and brain.
questions.question: How do mitochondria generate most cellular ATP?
options: By directly breaking glucose bonds without using the electron transport chain
By harnessing a proton gradient created by the electron transport chain to phosphorylate ADP
By capturing light energy like chloroplasts
By converting glucose directly to ATP without intermediate steps
questions.correctAnswer: By harnessing a proton gradient created by the electron transport chain to phosphorylate ADP
questions.explanation: The speaker describes ATP synthase using the electron-transport-generated proton gradient to produce ATP.

questions.prompt: Item 13: Sustainable Architecture and Green Buildings
questions.audioScript: Modern architecture increasingly incorporates sustainability through passive design and renewable energy. Buildings positioned to maximize natural light and ventilation reduce energy consumption. Green roofs insulate buildings while managing stormwater. Recycled and locally sourced materials minimize transportation impacts. Solar panels and wind turbines provide clean energy. Water recycling systems reduce consumption. These features create healthier occupant environments while reducing environmental …
options: footprints
impacts
consequences
effects
questions.explanation: The speaker specifically states sustainable features reduce environmental footprints.

questions.audioScript: Medieval castles served strategic defensive purposes in warfare. Stone walls could withstand siege weapons far better than wooden palisades. Multiple defensive layers including moats, walls, and towers provided overlapping fields of fire. Narrow windows called arrow slits allowed defenders to shoot while remaining protected. The keep provided a final defensive position if outer walls were breached. High walls prevented direct assault and made scaling extremely difficult. Castles dominated their territories militarily and politically for centuries.
questions.displayTranscript: Medieval castles served strategic offensive purposes in warfare. Stone walls could withstand siege weapons far better than wooden palisades. Multiple defensive layers including moats, walls, and towers provided overlapping fields of view. Narrow windows called gun slits allowed defenders to shoot while remaining protected. The dungeon provided a final defensive position if outer walls were breached. Low walls prevented direct assault and made scaling extremely difficult. Castles dominated their territories militarily and politically for centuries.
questions.explanation: Castles were defensive, used for fire control, had arrow slits and keeps, and had high walls for protection.

questions.audioScript: Evolution occurs through natural selection acting on genetic variation within populations. Organisms producing more offspring than the environment supports must compete for resources. Traits that improve survival and reproduction become more common across generations. Over millions of years, accumulated changes produce new species. Fossil records document transition forms showing evolutionary relationships. Genetic evidence confirms common ancestry across all living organisms. Evolution explains the diversity of life and shapes our understanding of biology.
questions.displayTranscript: Evolution occurs through artificial selection acting on genetic variation within populations. Organisms producing fewer offspring than the environment supports must compete for resources. Traits that decrease survival and reproduction become more common across generations. Over thousands of years, accumulated changes produce new species. Fossil records document transition forms showing revolutionary relationships. Chemical evidence confirms common ancestry across all living organisms. Evolution explains the simplicity of life and shapes our understanding of biology.
questions.explanation: Natural selection increases beneficial traits over millions of years through evolutionary relationships.
